summary:
Research handoff recording the fifth confirmed in-scope violation and a sourced extension for the other future types; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

Fifth finding confirmed: direct check 54e71939c4644eacbd929a505b3aac2a executed its fixed bytes as e69bc2007c144a7fb7e950e3827d2cb4 with the declarative prerequisite accepted matched, comparison_complete and witness_complete true, and the assertion violated — the future returned for an accepted Apply reported responded_after_shutdown false and shutdown_escape false, so caller_can_complete was false, while the same call on a served node completed. The blocking review issue (the Future.Error documentation promising ErrRaftShutdown among the errors a caller may see) was resolved as an independent scope boundary rather than by weakening the claim.

Product contents: the draft map (base version 18) adds a branch note to b-client-future recording the measured outcome and narrows the f-client-completion-escape unknown, which now records the sourced exposure of the other futures — verifyCh is buffered with capacity 64 so VerifyLeader can accept a future that shutdown then drops, while configurationChangeCh, bootstrapCh and userSnapshotCh are unbuffered and leadershipTransferCh holds one, narrowing their window — as a characterised but unexecuted extension. No trigger, guard, write, edge, requirement or previously accepted Surface changed, so the six violated scenarios, the two corroborating scenarios and all accepted results keep their original basis.

Run state: five in-scope violations, each confirmed with correspondence no_issue_found and no pending review work — batching-FSM ConfigurationStore delivery; heartbeat fast-path header gate (with measured vote suppression); TimeoutNow sender attribution (with measured vote granting); snapshot install log-tail alignment (with measured anchor rejection and a sourced reachability condition); and client future completion after shutdown (with the other future types characterised from source).

Remaining frontier: execution of the other futures' exposure; the four deployment-level premises (out-of-window heartbeat sender, unconfigured TimeoutNow sender, batching-FSM ConfigurationStore exemption, live-leader snapshot tail); the ReloadConfig, processHeartbeat-concurrency and transport TimeoutScale leads; and the still-unread in-memory snapshot store.
